title: Food, quantities and polite everyday exchanges

questions.prompt: Complete the request: « Je ___ un chocolat chaud, s'il vous plaît. »
questions.explanation: Je voudrais is a polite first-person conditional request.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct partitive for masculine singular café: « ___ café ».
questions.explanation: Du is the masculine singular partitive before café.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct partitive: « Je mange ___ soupe. »
questions.explanation: Soupe is feminine singular; de la indicates an unspecified quantity.

questions.prompt: Choose the article before the vowel in « ___ eau ».
questions.explanation: De l' precedes a vowel sound in eau.

questions.prompt: Complete a negative quantity: « Je ne bois pas ___ lait. »
questions.explanation: In a simple negation, partitive du generally becomes de.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct count: « Je prends ___ croissants. »
questions.explanation: Deux is a numeral used for countable plural croissants.

questions.prompt: Complete: « L'addition, ___ vous plaît. »
questions.explanation: S'il vous plaît is the standard polite expression.

questions.prompt: Which question asks for the price?
questions.explanation: Ça coûte combien asks how much an item costs.

questions.prompt: Choose the polite response to « Vous désirez ? »
questions.explanation: Je voudrais politely states what the customer wants.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le menu du jour propose une soupe et un sandwich. » What is offered?
questions.explanation: Une soupe et un sandwich are explicitly listed.

questions.prompt: Read: « La boulangerie ferme à dix-huit heures. » What time does it close?
questions.explanation: Dix-huit heures corresponds to 18:00 or 6 p.m.

questions.prompt: Read: « Il reste trois pommes, mais il n'y a plus de bananes. » Which fruit is unavailable?
questions.explanation: Il n'y a plus de bananes means no bananas remain.

questions.prompt: Read: « Maya préfère le thé sans sucre. » What does Maya avoid?
questions.explanation: Sans sucre means without sugar.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le plat coûte douze euros et la boisson trois euros. » What is the drink's price?
questions.explanation: La boisson trois euros explicitly prices the drink.

questions.prompt: Read: « Nous partageons une tarte après le déjeuner. » When is the tart eaten?
questions.explanation: Après le déjeuner indicates after lunch.

questions.prompt: Read: « Je suis allergique aux noix. » What is important to understand?
choices: The speaker has a nut allergy.
The speaker is asking for more nuts.
questions.explanation: Allergique aux noix communicates a dietary safety concern.

questions.prompt: Read: « Le serveur apporte deux verres d'eau. » How many glasses are brought?
questions.explanation: Deux verres d'eau means two glasses of water.

questions.prompt: Read: « Pour emporter » on a café sign. What service is offered?
questions.explanation: Pour emporter denotes an order intended to take away.

questions.prompt: You order a glass of water politely. Which request works?
choices: Un verre d'eau, s'il vous plaît.
Une verre du eau, s'il vous plaît.
Je suis eau, s'il vous plaît.
questions.explanation: Un verre d'eau is the idiomatic expression for a glass of water.

questions.prompt: A server asks « Sur place ou à emporter ? » You want to eat there. Choose the reply.
questions.explanation: Sur place means consuming the order at the establishment.

questions.prompt: You cannot eat nuts. Which sentence should you say before ordering?
choices: Je suis allergique au pain, donc ajoutez des noix.
Je suis allergique aux noix. Est-ce que ce plat en contient ?
Je veux beaucoup de noix, merci.
questions.explanation: The first option communicates the allergy and asks whether the dish contains nuts.

questions.prompt: A customer wants the bill. Which phrase is appropriate?
questions.explanation: L'addition is the restaurant bill.

questions.prompt: You want two baguettes rather than an unspecified quantity of bread.
questions.explanation: Deux explicitly counts two baguettes without a partitive.

questions.prompt: A café menu lists one sandwich at six euros. You buy two. What is the food total?
questions.explanation: Two sandwiches at six euros each cost twelve euros.

questions.prompt: You want to ask whether a soup is vegetarian. What do you ask?
choices: Est-ce que cette soupe est végétarienne ?
questions.explanation: The first question directly asks if the soup is vegetarian.

questions.prompt: The menu says « épuisé » beside the cake. What is the appropriate interpretation?
questions.explanation: Épuisé on a menu means the item is unavailable or sold out.

questions.prompt: A classmate confuses « du pain » with « deux pains ». Which explanation is correct?
choices: Du pain always means no bread.
Du pain is an unspecified amount; deux pains counts two loaves.
Both expressions always mean exactly two loaves.
questions.explanation: The partitive du differs from the numerical determiner deux.
